correctness.rationale: Between two successive fixed points (or the final endpoint), monotonicity and regressiveness force all nonroots to have a smaller parent in the same interval. As parent labels are nondecreasing, visiting vertices in a queue produces exactly the consecutive labels within each component. Conversely componentwise breadth-first labelling of any plane forest gives a nondecreasing regressive map, including across component boundaries. Each vertex takes exactly its edge-depth many iterates to reach its fixed root. Equality of two successive powers is equivalent to every orbit having reached its root, and depth-first parenthesis nesting is edge-depth plus one for a nonempty forest. The empty map is counted separately with depth zero. A depth-k forest is a sequence of roots with child forests of depth at most k-1, giving the stated formal-series recurrence with F_0=1/(1-z). Its first three iterates give the displayed coefficient formulas. A chain of k+1 vertices and n-k-1 singletons realizes each k, and at k=n-1 only the chain occurs. For fixed k the even-step path-graph walk counts give the stated squared spectral radius, with positive endpoint projection and no cancellation on even powers.
residual_risks: The displayed exponential growth is cumulative at fixed k. The verifier's depth routine uses the parent-depth recursion rather than an independent comparison of successive powers; the proof establishes that equality universally.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: If T_k(z) counts one-root maps of bounded stabilization depth, every general map is uniquely a sequence of shifted one-root interval maps, and it has bounded depth iff every component does; hence F_k=1/(1-T_k). The bounded-tree counts then pass to the full census and to Dyck height by standard encoding. evidence: The indexed author-abstract passage for Sönmez–Ünlü connects s-potent order-preserving maps with sole fixed point 1 to ordered trees of bounded depth. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An order-preserving map with sole fixed point 1 is regressive: an increasing first step would force an orbit to another fixed point. For these acyclic maps the conditions f^(m+1)=f^m and idempotence of f^m for m>=1 have the same threshold because all images must already consist of fixed points. This identifies the mathematical overlap for either of those conventions, without asserting which exact convention the older paper uses. The offset of one in Dyck height is just counting the root's parenthesis.

originality.rationale: The claimed novelty of the stabilization-depth distribution and its ordered-tree identification is not established. Substantive pre-2026 author-abstract evidence already connects the bounded-potency one-fixed-point class of order-preserving maps to bounded-depth ordered trees and reports generating functions. The one-fixed-point class with root 1 is exactly the one-component Catalan class before imposing the potency bound. The general forest claim reduces to those components, with the standard parentheses encoding and classical bounded-height enumeration. A distinct indexed finding directly gives the same breadth-first forest identification and a stronger joint rank/depth census whose marginal is the frozen census. This comparison demonstrates mathematical coverage and strong prior-work overlap, but does not prove that the older full text literally states the precise breadth-first algorithm or the Dyck formulation, and the later indexed finding is not evidence of earlier public priority.
residual_risks: Full texts of Sönmez–Ünlü and Yağcı–Korkmaz were not available in bounded lawful attempts, and Laradji–Umar and Solomon were not retrieved. The exact legacy exponent notation and explicitly published algorithm are not settled. The failure is based on substantive accessible coverage and lack of a substantiated distinct remainder, not those access limitations or a claim of historical priority.
